ai.definition: RAG pipelines in production, or Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines, are a method that combines the strengths of retrieval-based models and generative models to improve the efficiency and accuracy of information retrieval. In this approach, a retrieval model first fetches relevant documents from a knowledge base, which are then used by a generative model to produce context-aware responses.
ai.howItWorks: The process begins with a user query that is fed into a retrieval model. This model searches through a pre-indexed database or knowledge graph and selects the most relevant documents based on semantic similarity. These selected documents are then passed to a generative model, which uses them as context to produce a more accurate and coherent response compared to traditional generation models that do not have access to external information.
ai.problemSolved: RAG pipelines address the limitations of purely generative models by leveraging retrieval to incorporate factual knowledge into the generation process. This helps in reducing hallucinations, improving the relevance of generated content, and enhancing overall user satisfaction in applications like chatbots, virtual assistants, and AI agents.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing of RAG pipelines involves developing and optimizing both the retrieval and generative components. This includes fine-tuning pre-trained models for specific tasks, creating or sourcing a relevant knowledge base, and integrating these components into a cohesive system that can handle real-time queries efficiently.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts with selecting appropriate pre-trained language models as the basis for both retrieval and generation. These models are then fine-tuned on task-specific data to improve their performance. Next, a knowledge base is created or sourced, which includes structured and unstructured documents relevant to the domain of interest. Finally, these components are integrated into an RAG pipeline framework that can handle user queries and generate context-aware responses.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the initial investment in pre-trained models, the cost of creating or sourcing a knowledge base, computational resources required for fine-tuning models, and ongoing maintenance costs such as updates to the knowledge base and model optimizations.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook for RAG pipelines is positive, with increasing adoption in various applications. As more companies recognize the benefits of context-aware responses, we expect to see a growing market for RAG solutions.
ai.regulation: Regulations around data privacy and content accuracy will play a significant role in the deployment of RAG pipelines. Companies must ensure that their knowledge bases comply with relevant laws and ethical standards.
ai.risks: Risks include potential biases in the knowledge base, challenges in maintaining up-to-date information, and the risk of over-reliance on pre-trained models which may not be perfect for every use case.
ai.profitability: Profitability is likely to increase as more companies adopt RAG pipelines for their AI applications. The ability to provide more accurate and relevant responses can lead to better user experiences and potentially higher customer satisfaction, driving revenue growth.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will focus on improving the efficiency of knowledge base retrieval, enhancing model integration, and expanding the range of domains that RAG pipelines can effectively cover. Advancements in natural language processing and machine learning will also drive further improvements in performance and usability.

glossary.def: A method that combines retrieval with generation to create more context-aware responses.
A component of RAG pipelines responsible for fetching relevant documents from a knowledge base based on user queries.
A component of RAG pipelines that uses the retrieved documents as context to produce more accurate and coherent responses.
A repository of structured and unstructured documents relevant to a specific domain used in RAG pipelines for context-aware generation.

subsystems.name: Ingestion
subsystems.role: pulls raw content out of source systems and turns it into clean text.
parts: source connectors (wikis, file stores, ticketing systems, databases)

subsystems.name: Chunking and enrichment
subsystems.role: cuts documents into passages small enough to retrieve precisely.
parts: chunkers with overlap or semantic boundaries

subsystems.name: Indexing
subsystems.role: makes every chunk findable by meaning and by keyword.
parts: vector index (approximate nearest-neighbour, e.g. HNSW or IVF)
document store for the original text

subsystems.name: Retrieval
subsystems.role: turns a user question into the handful of passages that matter.

subsystems.name: Reranking and context assembly
subsystems.role: reorders candidates by true relevance and packs them into the prompt.

subsystems.name: Generation
subsystems.role: writes the answer using only the supplied passages.

subsystems.name: Evaluation and observability
subsystems.role: measures whether the pipeline is actually right.

buildSteps.title: Inventory the content
buildSteps.detail: List every source the answers must come from, and note which are clean text and which are scanned PDFs, spreadsheets or nested tables.

buildSteps.title: Parse and clean
buildSteps.detail: Extract text while keeping structure — headings, lists, table rows — and strip boilerplate such as navigation and footers.

buildSteps.title: Chunk with metadata
buildSteps.detail: Split each document into passages of a few hundred tokens, carrying source, date, section and access permissions with every chunk.

buildSteps.title: Build both indexes
buildSteps.detail: Run chunks through an embedding model into a vector index, and build a keyword index over the same text so exact terms, codes and names are still findable.

buildSteps.title: Wire the query path
buildSteps.detail: Rewrite the user question, apply permission filters, run dense and sparse search in parallel and merge the ranked lists.

buildSteps.title: Add reranking and packing
buildSteps.detail: Score the merged candidates with a cross-encoder, keep the best few, deduplicate and fit them into the model's context window.

buildSteps.title: Generate with citations
buildSteps.detail: Prompt the model to answer only from the supplied passages, attach source links, and return a clear 'not found' when the evidence is weak.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate offline
buildSteps.detail: Run a labelled question set and score retrieval separately from answer quality, so failures can be traced to the right stage.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and refresh
buildSteps.detail: Trace live requests, log failures and user feedback, re-embed changed documents incrementally, and re-tune chunk size or model when scores drift.

prerequisites.why: retrieval by meaning depends on mapping queries and passages into the same vector space.
exact comparison against millions of vectors would be too slow at interactive latency.
several retrieved passages plus the conversation must fit in one prompt.
cheap first-stage retrieval is noisy; reranking fixes much of the ordering.

prerequisites.tech: Robust document parsing for messy files
prerequisites.why: scanned pages, multi-column layouts and complex tables still lose information.
without reliable scoring, chunking and model choices are guesses rather than engineering decisions.

pathway.milestone: hybrid retrieval, reranking and citations as the standard production pattern
pathway.unlocks: assistants that answer from a known corpus and show their sources.

pathway.milestone: agentic retrieval that rewrites, decomposes and repeats searches before answering
pathway.unlocks: multi-hop questions that a single lookup cannot resolve.

pathway.milestone: structured retrieval over tables, knowledge graphs and databases alongside text
pathway.unlocks: numeric and relational questions, not just prose ones.

pathway.milestone: retrieval trained jointly with the generator, plus caching of stable context
pathway.unlocks: lower latency and fewer unsupported claims without hand-tuned pipelines.
